query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using a machine learning-based potential to generate reference configurations for thermodynamic integration can improve the representation of the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Solid and liquid states of multicomponent high-entropy alloys at and near their high melting temperatures
generation.intervention: Using a machine learning-based potential to generate reference configurations for thermodynamic integration
generation.conditions: High melting temperatures, multicomponent high-entropy alloys
generation.mechanism: Improved representation of atomic configurations leads to better reference-target phase-space overlap, reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved prediction of thermodynamic properties, such as melting temperature and phase stability
generation.boundary: Applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys with high melting temperatures, composition ranges where configurational entropy plays a significant role

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the performance of machine learning-based potentials with traditional EAM references in predicting thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine learning-based potentials do not show significant improvement over traditional EAM references in predicting thermodynamic properties, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: By accounting for the configurational entropy in addition to the mixing enthalpy, our ab initio-driven thermodynamic model achieves an accuracy up to 74% for predicting the phase stability of multicomponent alloys, surpassing existing empirical rules and free-energy models. The predictive power of the model could be further improved by the inclusion of vibrational effects, magnetic ordering, and short-range ordering, that have been neglected in the present model. All of these effects would significantly increase the computational cost and prevent the large scale search we have reported on. Nevertheless, alloys suggested by our model could be used to perform a more refined modeling including these effects within a possible tiered screening approach for HEA discovery.

The melting temperature is a crucial property of materials that determines their potential applications in different industrial fields. In this study, we used a deep neural network potential to describe the structure of high-entropy (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x carbonitrides (HECN) in both solid and liquid states. This approach allows us to predict heating and cooling temperatures depending on the nitrogen content to determine the melting temperature and analyze structure changes from atomistic point of view. A steady increase in nitrogen content leads to increasing melting temperature, with a maximum approaching for 25% of nitrogen in the HECN. A careful analysis of pair correlations, together with calculations of entropy in the considered liquid phases of HECNs allows us to explain the origin of the nonlinear enhancement of the melting temperature with increasing nitrogen content. The maximum melting temperature of 3580 ± 30 K belongs to (TiZrTaHfNb)C0.75N0.25 composition. The improved melting behavior of high-entropy compounds by the addition of nitrogen provides a promising way towards modification of thermal properties of functional and constructional materials.

It is important to consider that the metal carbide precursors have very strong covalent/ionic bonds, and are therefore enthalpy stabilized. However, the same might not be the case for their mixture. In fact, a statistical analysis of the AFLOW.org enthalpies indicates that the gain in formation enthalpy by adding mixing species, ΔHf(N + 1) − ΔHf(N), decreases with N, and can easily be overcome by the monotonic increase in entropy-gain for the disordered systems (to go from order to complete or partial disorder). In the AFLOW analysis, the threshold between low- and high-entropy systems is around four mixing species. To have completely entropy-stabilized materials, five mixing species are required (similar to the Entropy-Stabilized Oxides). For carbides in which only the metal-sublattice is randomly populated, five metals should be enough to achieve carbide entropy stabilization, especially at equi-composition. Notably, if other sublattices were also allowed to contain disorder, (e.g., reciprocal systems like TaxHf1−xC1−y,), then the overall number of species might reduce.
